explanation: Warm greetings, including handshakes, embraces, and cheek-kissing among close friends or relatives, are common between people of the same gender in the UAE, reflecting Bedouin hospitality traditions. Greeting someone of the opposite gender this way is different: unless they are a close relative, it's best to wait and see whether they extend a hand or cheek first.
local_tip: With someone of the same gender who greets you warmly, mirror their lead; with the opposite gender, default to a verbal greeting and a nod unless they initiate physical contact.

also_check.note: Cheek-kissing (la bise) is a standard greeting between friends and acquaintances of any gender, with the number of kisses varying by region.
Physical greetings like cheek-kissing are not customary; a bow is the expected greeting instead.
Cheek-kissing is common among the same gender, but cross-gender physical greetings in public are avoided.

sources.title: A Handshake is Worth 1000 Words: Body Language in Dubai Business Culture
